analyst_observations: The skill's biggest win is on Eval 2 (confirmation sound): with the skill, all 4 voice pipeline locations were found; without it, only 2 of 4 were found, and no warning about incomplete changes was given. This is the core value proposition — the skill's architecture knowledge prevents incomplete changes.

Eval 1 (wakeword) passed all assertions both ways, but the without-skill run took 34% longer (117s vs 87s) and used 12% more tokens (42k vs 37k) because it needed extensive file exploration that the skill's context made unnecessary.

Eval 3 (settings page) passed all assertions both ways, but qualitatively the with-skill response is stronger: it recommends the cleaner dedicated RPC approach and explicitly rejects CommandRequest abuse, while the without-skill version recommends CommandRequest as its primary approach.
The with-skill runs are consistently faster (avg 96s vs 109s) because the architectural context reduces exploration time.
